title: Client adapter wishlist synthesis: session-resume, streaming guardrails, and language gap catalog
creator: Sofia Patel
description: Synthesize incoming enterprise and partner requests for client adapter features into a prioritized wishlist and concrete engineering tickets. Focus areas: robust session-resume semantics for resumable streaming connections, standardized auth patterns across language bindings (token refresh, rotating credentials), and streaming guardrails (backpressure, cancel semantics, reconnect heuristics). Outcome: a runnable prioritization rubric + scoped tickets for v1 SDK adapters and a short-term compatibility shim for enterprise customers who need immediate fixes.
acceptance_criteria: A consolidated wishlist document listing top 12 customer requests with source links and representative customer examples
A prioritization rubric scored by cost-to-ship, customer-revenue-exposure, security risk, and UX friction
Scoped engineering tickets (ENG-xxxxx) created for top 5 items with estimates and owner assignments
A short-term compatibility shim proposal for session-resume that can be implemented as a gateway-layer change
Design sketches for streaming API ergonomics for 3 target languages (Python, JS, Java) and a proposed canonical behavior spec
proposed_solution: Deliver a two-track approach: (1) immediate gateway-backed compatibility shim that adds session-resume tokens and server-side reconnect glue for the highest-impact customers; (2) medium-term SDK adapter changes to standardize auth refresh hooks, expose backpressure/cancel callbacks, and implement resumable session tokens in the client event loop. Pair PM with ENG runtime and DevEx leads to align on telemetry and error semantics.
tradeoffs: Shim approach minimizes customer downtime but increases long-term maintenance burden unless replaced by native SDK support
Standardizing on a single resumable token format requires coordination across Dedicated and Private deployments (adds rollout complexity)
Prioritizing enterprise-facing auth patterns may delay the broader multi-language ergonomics work for community users
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (2 weeks): gather and validate customer use-cases, run intake interviews for top 6 customers. Phase 2 (4 weeks): implement gateway shim prototype and run with 2 pilot customers under dedicated routing. Phase 3 (8 weeks): land SDK adapter changes in Python and JS with feature flags, add telemetry dashboards to Console. Phase 4: expand to Java/Go and deprecate shim once native flows are stable.
